title: Outcome vocabulary on every run
description:
Add `outcome` to `ProcedureRun` with exactly five values: `acted` (it did the work), `nothing` (it looked and there was nothing to do), `asked` (it raised a question for a person and stopped), `failed` (it could not do the work; nothing half-done is left as if done), `unknown` (it started and no result was recorded). Add a short `outcomeReason` code, plus `automationId`, `responsibility`, `subjectKind`, `subjectId`, `subjectVersion` and `rung` (the rung it ran under). `runStatus` keeps the mechanics (`waiting`, `queued`, `started`, `finished`); `outcome` is set only when a run finishes or is settled. The runner writes both. The CLI and console show each outcome as a word with a mark, never colour alone. Delivery attempts use the same words for the same things (`started`, then `sent`, `refused` or `unknown`). Existing runs are not rewritten; a run without an outcome shows "recorded before outcomes".

**Acceptance criteria**
- A finished run always has one of the five outcomes.
- A run that looked and found nothing records `nothing` with a reason code; it is not a failure.
- `papyrus automations runs` and the console show the outcome in words with a mark.
- No existing run is rewritten.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- run-outcomes.feature: a run that does its work is `acted`; a run with nothing to do is `nothing` with a reason; a run that raises a review request is `asked`; a procedure error is `failed`; an older run shows 'recorded before outcomes'.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Amplify data schema: new optional fields on `ProcedureRun` (no index in this task). Runner image.

**Part of:** Wake contract and run outcomes. Slice code A1 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
